messages.author: 14ce58f9c4879902
messages.subject: Factor Scores from repeated measures
parts:
Dear all,

How would you estimate factor scores from longitudinal data for later use in a model (if multiple indicatior is not an option)? I see some different approaches and would be happy for your advise.
  1. lavPredict on seperate models, one for each construct, one at each timepoint
  2. lavPredict on seperate 'full measurement' models, one at each timepoint
  3. establish measurment invariance of the full measurment model and use lavPredict on the most strict model
Also, which estimation method would you use? Note that some constructs in the measurment model are higher-order.

Best,
Lucas Maunz

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Factor Scores from repeated measures
parts:
Definitely 3, if you have to use factor scores (instead of sam(), for example).  Comparing factor scores across occasions relies on (at least) the same assumptions as comparing latent parameters in a longitudinal CFA/SEM.  Method 1 would also inflate the correlation among repeated measures, to the degree that the unique factors (residuals) are correlated over time.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Factor Scores from repeated measures
parts:
Hi everybody,

I want to analyze the effect of an intervention on a construct mediated by another construct, as in the model below.

'# 0 stands for data collected before the intervention, while 1, 2, and 3 stands for data after the baseline. Construct F has 6 indicators, while I has 5.
# intervention is dichotomous (0 = control, 1 = experimental group)
F1 ~ F0 + intervention
F2 ~ F1 + intervention
F3 ~ F2 + intervention

I0 ~ F0
I1 ~ F1 + I0 + intervention
I2 ~ F2 + I1 + intervention
I3 ~ F3 + I2 + intervention'

However, due to difficulties inherent in the intervention, I have only 40 participants (30 with complete data) and this model does not converge even when I diminish the number of parameters to be estimated by adding constraints to make it time invariant and ignoring the group. Moreover, as far as I understand, I can't use data in the long format, with time predicting the LVs, because this wouldn't consider the dependency of the observations.

Do you have any suggestions of how I could test this model considering the measurement errors? I was thinking that I could sum the items and use the reliability coefficient in a path analysis, but I have no knowledge if this has already been explored.

I would appreciate your attention.
Yago
